traditions.n: Henna: rituals, aesthetic and social practices
traditions.r: Arab states and North Africa (UAE, Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Mauritania, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Tunisia, Yemen)
traditions.p: ancient to present; UNESCO Representative List 2024
traditions.d: Henna body art and rites such as the Night of the Henna, inscribed by UNESCO on a 16-state nomination.
traditions.tech: leaf powder mixed to a paste, applied by stick or syringe, left to stain
traditions.auth: Real henna stains reddish-brown and darkens over a day or two; 'black henna' that stains black fast contains PPD and can cause severe allergy and scarring.

traditions.d: South Asian henna art on hands, wrists, forearms and feet for weddings, religious festivals and family ceremonies.
traditions.tech: paste piped from a plastic cone, brush or stick; dries, cracks and is left to stain
traditions.mat: henna powder, water or lemon, oils
traditions.auth: Body-art-quality henna is finely sifted; avoid PPD 'black henna' (Florida Department of Health, FDA warnings).

traditions.r: Egypt, Middle East, North and West Africa
traditions.d: Mineral eye cosmetic worn by Egyptians of all classes and spread through Arabia, North Africa and West Africa.
traditions.tech: crushing mineral to fine powder; applied with a stick
traditions.mat: stibnite (antimony sulfide); modern often galena (lead sulfide), charcoal
ctr: Hausa, Fulani, Tuareg and Yoruba peoples
traditions.auth: Many traditional kohls contain lead; the FDA warns against kohl, kajal, al-kahal, surma, tiro, tozali and kwalli for lead poisoning risk.

traditions.d: Soot-based kajal and mineral surma worn by women and children, also against the evil eye and in classical dance.
traditions.tech: kajal: soot from burning oil or ghee mixed with oil; surma: ground mineral
traditions.mat: soot, ghee, camphor, sandalwood; galena or other minerals
traditions.auth: Both have been linked to chemical toxicity, especially lead; prefer products with ingredient lists.

traditions.d: Red powders marking marital status in the hair parting (sindoor) and worn as forehead marks (kumkum).
traditions.tech: turmeric dried and powdered with slaked lime, alum or lime turns it red
traditions.mat: turmeric, alum, slaked lime; historically vermilion or red lead
traditions.auth: Herbal turmeric-based powder is non-toxic; some commercial sindoor contains lead (FDA warning on Swad sindoor).

traditions.r: India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and diaspora
traditions.d: Forehead dot worn by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists, red or maroon after sindoor and kumkum, now often a sticker.
traditions.tech: painted with powder, or self-adhesive felt or metal
traditions.mat: kumkum, sindoor, lac, felt, thin metal
traditions.auth: Traditional bindi is painted; lac tikli preceded modern stickers.

traditions.d: Red dye painted on hands and feet at weddings and festivals.
traditions.tech: applied with cotton swab or brush
traditions.mat: red lac; now mainly synthetic dye
traditions.auth: Natural alta is lac-based; most current alta is synthetic.

notes: Planned kinds all kept: Kumkum & sindoor (old k30 'Skin paint'; its Parul Garg model kept in m with old source), Kohl & surma, Henna, Bindi, Face & body paint. Added kind Alta (red hand/foot dye, Wikipedia-sourced) as a missing traditional adornment. Tilaka added as an archetype under Kumkum & sindoor rather than a kind. Kajal pencils (commercial) left to Eyeliner; hair henna left to Hair dye. Wolfe FX and Diamond FX sourced from a face-paint retailer page (Jest Paint) because no maker page was retrieved; founding years for Snazaroo, Wolfe FX and Diamond FX unknown, left blank. Ben Nye kept as m only (no specific face-paint line confirmed). No baby tag: face paint as a kind is not made specifically for children (Snazaroo brand is child-focused). Black henna/PPD and lead in kohl/sindoor recorded as tradition authenticity notes, not kinds. FDA kohl page and PubMed bindi-leukoderma paper were not retrieved, so not cited. No moves.
